ud3.6:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha, in Bamboo Wood, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
ud3.6:1.3: Then at that time venerable Pilindivaccha accosted monks with words of contempt.
ud3.6:1.4: Then many monks went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side. While sat on one side those monks said this to the Fortunate One:
ud3.6:1.5: “Venerable Pilindivaccha, reverend Sir, accosts monks with words of contempt.”
ud3.6:2.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed a certain monk, (saying):
ud3.6:2.2: “Please go, monk, and with my word address the monk Pilindivaccha, (saying):
ud3.6:2.4: “Yes, reverend Sir,” said that monk, and after replying to the Fortunate One, he went to venerable Pilindivaccha, and after going, he said this to venerable Pilindivaccha:
ud3.6:3.1: “Yes, friend,” said venerable Pilindivaccha, and after replying to that monk, he went to the Fortunate One, after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sat on one side the Fortunate One said this to venerable Pilindivaccha:
ud3.6:3.2: “Is it true, as it seems, Vaccha, that you accost monks with words of contempt?”
ud3.6:4.1: Then the Fortunate One, after applying his mind to venerable Pilindivaccha’s previous lives, addressed the monks, (saying):
ud3.6:4.2: “You should not be offended, monks, at the monk Vaccha,
ud3.6:4.3: it is not with hatred on the inside, monks, that Vaccha accosts the monks with words of contempt.
ud3.6:4.4: For the monk Vaccha, monks, for five hundred lives has been reborn in a brāhmaṇa family without interruption,
ud3.6:4.5: for a long time he has been one who has accosted (others) with words of contempt,
ud3.6:4.6: because of this Vaccha accosted the monks with words of contempt.”
ud3.6:5.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud3.6:6.1: “In whom dwells no deceit and no conceit,
ud3.6:6.2: He who is free from lust, unselfish, not yearning,
ud3.6:6.3: Who has dispelled anger, who is himself completely emancipated,
ud3.6:6.4: He is a brāhmaṇa, he is an ascetic, he is a monk.”
